intro.title: What does Exyconn build for professional services firms?
intro.definition: is software that handles the non-billable work around client engagements, such as proposals, scheduling, document chasing, first drafts and timesheets, so a firm's people spend more of their week on work clients pay for. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on your CRM, practice management or PSA tool, accounting software and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Partners keep approval of every proposal, deliverable and invoice.

benefits.title: Why firms are doing this now

items.text: The firm that replies first with a clear scope and fee often wins the work.
Most reports, engagement letters and proposals start from something the firm has already written.
Every unrecorded call or email is time that will never reach an invoice.
Senior people spend evenings on admin that a junior or a system could do.
Fixed-fee work only pays if you can see an engagement running over while it is still running.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a firm's non-billable hours actually go
props.lede: Managing partners at accounting firms, consultancies and design studios describe the same week. The expertise is billable; the work around it is not.

items.title: Proposals written from a blank page
items.text: Each enquiry needs a scope, an approach, a team and a fee. Partners rebuild them late at night from old proposals they half remember, and slow replies lose work.

items.title: Calendar back-and-forth
items.text: Kick-off calls, reviews and site visits need three or four people from both sides. Finding a slot takes a thread of emails before any work is done.

items.title: Chasing clients for information
items.text: Bank statements, invoices, drawings, access to systems. Staff send the same reminder several times, and deadlines slip on the one thing still missing.

items.title: Timesheets filled in on Friday
items.text: People reconstruct the week from memory, so short calls and quick reviews disappear. Invoices go out late, narratives are thin and write-offs follow.

items.title: Past work you cannot find
items.text: The firm has done this kind of audit, feasibility study or migration before. Finding the deliverable means asking around until someone remembers the folder.

items.title: Profitability known too late
items.text: Utilisation and margin by client are worked out in a spreadsheet after the quarter closes, when a fixed-fee engagement has already overrun.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your fee earners

items.title: Enquiry intake and proposals
items.text: Replies to enquiries from your website and email, asks the scoping questions your partners would ask and logs the lead in your CRM. It then drafts a proposal from your templates and past engagements for a partner to edit and send.

items.title: Meetings and scheduling
items.text: Finds a time that works for your team and the client from shared calendars, sends the invite with an agenda and the documents to read, and reschedules when someone drops out.

items.title: Document drafting and review
items.text: Produces first drafts of engagement letters, reports, minutes and client memos from your templates and working papers, and checks drafts against your house style and review checklist before a senior signs off.

items.title: Timesheets and billing
items.text: Suggests time entries from calendars, calls, emails and documents worked on, matched to the right client and engagement in your PSA or practice tool. Approved time becomes draft invoices in your accounting software.

items.title: Search over past work
items.text: Answers questions such as 'have we done a transfer pricing study for a pharma client?' from your document store and CRM, returning the deliverables, the team and links to the files each person is allowed to open.

items.title: Utilisation and profitability
items.text: Combines timesheets, fees and costs into utilisation by person and margin by client and engagement each week, and warns the engagement lead when a fixed-fee job passes its budgeted hours.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a 25-person accounting and advisory firm
props.lede: A Tuesday in filing season. Each moment lights the part of the firm the agent is working on.

moments.title: A kick-off call, booked without a thread
moments.text: A new audit client wants to meet this week. The agent finds an hour when the partner, the manager and the client's CFO are all free and sends the invite with the information request attached.

moments.title: An enquiry becomes a draft proposal
moments.text: A logistics company asks about outsourcing its monthly bookkeeping and payroll. The agent asks about transaction volumes and headcount, logs the lead and puts a draft proposal in the partner's inbox.

moments.title: Last year's work, found in a minute
moments.text: A manager asks whether the firm has prepared a due-diligence report for a manufacturing acquisition before. The agent returns two past reports and the names of the people who worked on them.

moments.title: A management letter, first draft done
moments.text: From the audit working papers and last year's letter, the agent drafts the management letter points. The manager rewrites two of them and sends it to the partner for review.

moments.title: Timesheets that fill themselves
moments.text: Each person gets suggested entries for the day's meetings, calls and files, already matched to clients. A short call with a payroll client that would have been forgotten is on the list.

moments.title: An overrun flagged before it grows
moments.text: The weekly utilisation report shows a fixed-fee tax engagement at 90% of its hours with a month to go. The engagement lead gets a note to talk to the client about scope.

items.question: Will this replace our junior staff?
items.answer: No. It takes admin off everyone's week: chasing documents, booking meetings, filling timesheets and producing first drafts. Juniors still do the analysis and seniors still review it, with more of their time spent on work the client pays for.

items.question: Which CRM, practice management and accounting tools does it work with?
items.answer: Any tool with an API or a reliable export: CRMs, PSA and practice management tools, timesheet apps, accounting software such as Tally, Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Xero, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. In the first week we confirm what your setup allows the agent to read and write.

items.question: How is client data kept confidential?
items.answer: Client files stay in your own document store or a private environment set up for the firm and are not used to train public models. The agent follows your folder and client permissions, every action is logged, and the setup follows the DPDP Act 2023 in India and the GDPR for clients in Europe.

items.question: Can it work with clients who prefer other languages?
items.answer: Yes. It can message clients in Hindi and other Indian languages or in the language they write in, while deliverables are drafted in the language you choose and reviewed by your team.

items.question: What happens when a draft or time entry is wrong?
items.answer: Nothing it produces goes out on its own: proposals, deliverables and invoices are approved by a person, and time entries are suggestions. Corrections are tracked and used to adjust templates and matching rules.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on firm size, the number of jobs automated and the tools involved. Most firms start with two jobs, often proposals and timesheets; tell us about your firm and we'll send a fixed quote for that first phase.
